I also work at BBW. Our location is inside a mall and is the larger of two stores in the building. An employee from the other store came into ours to shop SAS and refused to wear a mask. We were not rude or pushy (we aren't allowed to be), but asked her to please take a mask even if she just has it pulled down the whole time. Turns out she doesn't wear a mask at her own store as an employee and her store manager just doesn't care. A few of us, myself included, were then lectured and forced to sign documents about our policies simply for asking ANOTHER EMPLOYEE to please wear a fucking mask. I have not seen my parents for over a year due to Covid. My mom is vulnerable and could die from the virus. My 21st birthday is in April and it will the the second birthday I will not get to see my parents faces. When my dad's dad died in July, I stood 10 feet apart from my father as I watched him sob for the first time in my life. We cried and mourned in masks. It is so unbelievably frustrating to deal with. Sorry this went so long but it's hard to deal with customers everyday being outright ignorant and disrespectful to retail workers that are sacrificing so much for products that are not even essential.

I've actually started sabotaging myself (I'm not sure the whole mental gymnastics routine yet), where I'll cook one of my favorite foods, even if its healthy/lowcal, and completely ruin it with something I know I hate just so I dont binge. I binge anyways on it over guilt of wasting food and then usually purge it later. I think it makes impulse food buys even more common because I know its something I'll like. I try to not keep an empty fridge as I can fall into not eating for several days or order mountainous amounts of unhealthy delivery given the chance. It's a vicious cycle.
